title: What is the difference between {{ }} and {!! !!} in laravel blade files?
author: Stefan Bogdanescu

content:
Title: Understanding Differences Between {{ }} and {!! !!} in Laravel Blade Files Body: In the world of web development, incorporating PHP code into HTML files is a common practice to ensure dynamic content rendering on web pages. Laravel, being one of the most popular frameworks, uses Blade templating engine for handling this task. One of the main concerns when working with Blade is understanding and differentiating between two specific syntaxes: {{ }} and {!! !!}. 1. Understanding {{ }}

{{ }} is a native feature in Laravel's blade file, designed to handle HTML and PHP code seamlessly. The purpose of this syntax is to safely output any variables and data without worrying about the potential risks of inserting unescaped HTML tags or other malicious codes from user inputs. Think of {{ }} as a built-in method for preventing cross-site scripting (XSS) attacks.

{{ $name }} // Outputs text inside $name variable without worrying about XSS
2. Understanding {!! !!}

On the other hand, {!! !!} is a special syntax that allows you to output any raw HTML or PHP code directly in your Blade files. The main purpose of this syntax is to escape HTML tags and prevent Laravel from parsing them. This comes in handy when dealing with complex HTML structures that require precise rendering without interference from the framework.

{!! <div>This text will be rendered as-is, including HTML tags</div> !!} // Outputs entire HTML code inside tags without parsing
3. Differences between {{ }} and {!! !!}

These two syntaxes may seem similar at first glance but have different purposes. The primary difference is the level of escaping they provide. {{ }} takes care of escaping HTML tags and other potentially harmful user inputs, protecting your application from malicious code injections. On the contrary, {!! !!} allows you to bypass this protection and output raw HTML or PHP code without modification.

{!! <div>This text will be escaped, preserving HTML tags</div> !!} // Outputs entire HTML code with tags unchanged
4. Best Practices for Using {{ }} and {!! !!}

To ensure the security and maintainability of your Laravel application, follow these best practices:

- Always use {{ }} when working with variables and data output in Blade files to prevent XSS attacks and unescaped HTML tags. - Use {!! !!} only when you have a clear reason for not using the built-in escaping feature of {{ }}. This is primarily when you want to include raw HTML or complex PHP code directly in your template without interference from Laravel. Conclusion:

With this detailed explanation, you now understand the fundamental differences between {{ }} and {!! !!} in Laravel's Blade files. Always use {{ }} for secure data output and escaping to prevent potential security issues. However, if there's a genuine need for raw HTML or PHP code rendering, use {!! !!}. Remember to adopt best practices when working with these syntaxes to ensure the integrity of your application.
